title: Jesus didn’t choose random words.
paragraphs: Jesus didn’t choose random words.
When He said, “I am the vine,” He was revealing something most people still miss.

Not about theology.
Not about religion.
But about how life with God actually works.

Because a vine is not admired…
It’s depended on.
And that changes everything.
In Gospel of John 15:5, Jesus says:
Let that sink in.

Not some things.
Not less things.
Nothing.

That’s not exaggeration.
That’s reality from Heaven’s perspective.
Most people think spiritual growth is about trying harder.

Praying more.
Disciplining yourself more.
Fixing your habits.
And those things matter…

But Jesus never said,
“Strive harder to produce fruit.”

He said,
“Remain in Me.”

Because fruit is not the result of pressure.
It’s the result of connection.
A branch doesn’t strain to produce grapes.

It doesn’t wake up anxious thinking,
“Am I growing enough today?”
It simply stays connected to the vine.
And life flows naturally.
Here’s the part that should wake us up:
Branches don’t die the moment they disconnect.
They wither slowly.
And that’s how many people drift from God.

Not through rebellion…
But through quiet disconnection.
It starts small.

You skip time with God because you’re busy.
You stop listening as closely.
You rely more on your own strength.
Nothing feels dramatic.

No alarm bells.
No sudden collapse.
Just a slow fading.

Less sensitivity.
Less peace.
Less clarity.
Until one day you realize:
You’re still active… but no longer alive.
Jesus wasn’t just giving comfort in this passage.
He was giving a warning.

Because it is possible to look like a branch…
But not actually be connected.
And the most dangerous part?

You can stay around spiritual things
while being disconnected from the Source.

You can know Scripture…
but not remain in Him.

You can serve…
but not abide.

You can appear fruitful…
but be slowly drying out inside.
“Remain in Me.”
That word remain means to stay, to dwell, to continue.

Not visit occasionally.
Not check in when life gets hard.
Stay.

Because connection is not an event.
It’s a lifestyle.
And here’s a truth many people overlook:
The vine never disconnects from the branch.
The invitation is always open.
The life is always available.

The question is never,
“Is Jesus still the source?”
The question is:
Are you still connected?
And when you are…
Fruit happens.

Not forced.
Not manufactured.
But natural.

Love grows.
Peace stabilizes.
Wisdom sharpens.
Character deepens.
Not because you mastered life…
But because His life is flowing through you.
But when you disconnect…
You don’t just lose fruit.
You lose life.

Because Christianity was never meant to be lived
from your own strength.

It was designed to be lived
from His.
So here’s the real question:

Not “Are you doing enough?”
Not “Are you trying harder?”
But…
“Am I still remaining?”

Because everything changes
based on that one answer.

“A branch doesn’t produce fruit by effort…
but by attachment.”
“Disconnection rarely feels dangerous… until the fruit is gone.”
“You don’t lose life all at once… you drift from it slowly.”

“God is not asking for more performance…
He’s asking for deeper connection.”

If you feel dry…
if you feel distant…
if you feel like something is missing…
The answer is not to try harder.
It’s to return.
Reconnect.
Remain.
Because the vine is still alive.
And it’s still calling you.

Engagement Question:
What is one area of your life where you know you need to reconnect with God right now?
